title: Revealing the Discrepancy Between Ecosystem Service Flows and Public Perception in Heavily Impacted Lowland Rivers of Armenia
content:
ABSTRACT

River ecosystems are increasingly vulnerable to intensified human pressures associated with population growth and rising living standards, leading to structural changes and altered ecosystem service (ES) provision. The lower course of the Hrazdan River (Armenia) exemplifies these impacts, as it flows through Yerevan, the capital city, and receives substantial inputs of largely untreated wastewater. To assess resulting changes in ES, this study applies a multi-method approach combining field-based ecological assessments with social survey research. This integrated framework enables the comparison of actual ES flows with stakeholder perceptions, capturing both biophysical conditions and societal values. Results reveal a marked discrepancy between perceived and actual ES provision. While regulating and maintenance services are relatively highly prioritised by stakeholders, many essential ecosystem functions remain poorly understood, indicating significant knowledge gaps and limited public engagement. At the same time, the availability and quality of key services are severely degraded, contributing to tensions between stakeholders and decision-makers. These findings point to persistent management challenges, including mismatches between top–down governance and bottom–up engagement. The study highlights the importance of integrating ecological data with social perspectives to support more effective, inclusive and conservation-oriented management strategies for heavily impacted river systems.
